title.narrative: MEII Swedish Guarantee Facility 2 Admin + Technical Assistance 2025-2027

description.narrative:
Det gåvofinansierade tekniska biståndsprogrammet genom MEII har ett dubbelt syfte: 1) tekniskt bistånd och kapacitetsuppbyggnad, 2) förvaltning av den svenska garantifaciliteten.
MEII-programmet för teknisk assistans (Tamweeli) arbetar med direkt tekniskt stöd till mikro-, små- och medelstora företag (MSMEs) för att förstärka deras redovisningskapacitet och finansiella förmåga (på engelska benämnt ”financial literacy”) samt stärkt krisberedskap hos företag. Genom förstärkt kapacitet hos företagare att presentera sitt företag förbättras deras chanser att få ett lån och utvidga sin verksamhet. MEII prioriterar kvinnodrivna/-ägda företag och samarbetar med lokala handelskammare och fackföreningar. Det tekniska stödet inkluderar också en matchningsplattform där entreprenörer anonymt kan presentera sina finansiella behov för flera finansiella institut, inklusive banker, leasingföretag, aktieinvesterare och mikrofinansinstitut.
Vidare kommer det föreslagna bidraget också att finansiera MEII: s förvaltning av den svenska garantifaciliteten (SGF2) (PLANit ID 11275). Garantifaciliteten är upprättad av Sida och Middle East Investment Initiative (MEII). Den är utformad för att öka tillgången till finansiering av MSME i de marginaliserade områdena östra Jerusalem, Gaza, Hebron och Västbankens område C. Under SGF2 utfärdar Sida en garanti till MEII, som uppgår till mellan 29 miljoner USD. MEII, som arbetar som intermediär mellan Sida och de deltagande finansiella instituten (FI), använder Sidas garanti till att garantera de deltagande FI som kan placera godtagbara lån under garantin.

The grant funded technical assistance program through MEII has a two-folded purpose: 1) technical assistance and capacity building, 2) management of the Swedish Guarantee Facility (SGF2).
The MEII technical assistance program (Tamweeli) works with direct technical assistance to Micro- Small and Medium sized Enterprises (MSMEs), to strengthen their accounting capabilities, financial literacy and crisis preparedness. MEII’s capacity building works to equip entrepreneurs with the capacity to confidently present their business’ financial reports and thereby improve their chances of getting a loan and expanding their business. MEII is trying to give priority and preferential treatment to female-run businesses and has collaboration with local chambers of commerce and unions. The technical assistance also includes a matchmaking platform where entrepreneurs anonymously can present their financial needs to multiple financial intermediaries including banks, leasing companies, equity investors, and microfinance institutions.
Furthermore, the contribution will also finance MEII’s management of the Swedish Guarantee Facility (SGF2) (PLANit ID 11275). The guarantee facility is set up by Sida and the Middle East Investment Initiative (MEII). It builds on experience from the first phase of the SGF and is designed to increase access to finance of MSMEs in the marginalized areas of East Jerusalem, Gaza, Hebron and Area C of the West Bank. Under SGF2, Sida issues a guarantee to MEII, worth USD 29 million. MEII, who works as an intermediary between Sida and the participating financial institutions (FIs), extends the Sida guarantee to the FIs who may place eligible loans under the guarantee.

The overall Swedish engagement with MEII in Palestine is designed to support private sector activity in the marginalized economies of East Jerusalem, the Gaza Strip, and Area C of the West Bank under the two interlinked contributions: the SGF2 and the Tamweeli TA program.
By providing credit guarantee coverage, FIs will continue to explore marginalized areas and new banking clients. Ultimately, by developing the financial capacity of MSMEs, the program hopes to encourage financial transparency that leads to better governance, which will result in greater access to finance, economic growth, development, and employment in the MSME sector. Therefore, by intervening at the supply and demand level, SGF2 and the TAP provide a holistic intervention which aims to meet the impact objective to strengthen Palestinian MSMEs capacities´ to become better managed and more creditworthy, thereby enhancing their likelihood of securing capital and improving their resilience to economic shocks.
According to the program Results Matrix the proposed Tamweeli program has three principal objectives on Outcome level:
- Improved financial literacy, transparency and E&S practices of Palestinian MSMEs
- Improved MSME loan requests, matching with financial institutions and access to finance facilitated
- Retained private sector productive capacity
These Outcomes are measured by a battery of indicators on Impact and Output level and concretized with direct target figures.
